name: shared_buffers
description: Sets the amount of memory the database server uses for shared memory buffers. It is the primary component of PostgreSQL memory architecture.
tuning_tips: If you have a dedicated database server with 1GB or more of RAM, a reasonable starting value is 25% of the memory. Setting it significantly higher than 40% of RAM is usually unlikely to improve performance because PostgreSQL also relies on the OS cache.
official_snippet: If you have a dedicated database server with 1GB or more of RAM, a reasonable starting value for shared_buffers is 25% of the memory in your system. (Source: PostgreSQL Documentation)
